sections.heading: The Wharton AI Advantage
sections.text: We prepare learners to be leaders who use AI with the knowledge, judgment, and accountability their career stage demands. From pre-college through senior leadership, our faculty teach, research, and engage across the full continuum—creating a feedback loop that informs what we teach, how we teach, and how AI is applied in business and society.

sections.heading: Erika H. James
sections.text: “As AI continues to commoditize the world’s access to information, leaders need to prioritize the human skills AI can’t replicate. Things like sense-making, judgement, consensus-building, and above all, accountability. At Wharton, we believe people have and will continue to be essential to business’ ability to positively impact society. In this moment, we must make sure we don’t lose sight of humanity as AI becomes even more embedded in how we learn, work, and live.” — Dean, The Wharton School

sections.eyebrow: Wharton faculty teach and research across every stage.
sections.heading: Your AI Leadership Journey
sections.text: AI’s role grows with your leadership responsibility: a tutor and spark before college, a co-pilot before your career begins, a workflow partner in early and mid-career, and a strategic lever in the executive suite. Wharton faculty teach and research across all programs.

sections.heading: Faculty insight moves between research, the classroom, and practice
sections.text: Wharton has always been an innovator and early mover, and our approach to AI is no different. Our world-class faculty teach learners at every stage, from pre-college students to seasoned executives. They see firsthand how people and organizations are using AI to create value—and where the most consequential questions, opportunities, and risks are emerging. Those insights move between research, the classroom, and the world of practice, strengthening learning at every stage. Wharton is where ambitious students, scholars, and leaders come to understand AI’s impact on business and society—and help shape what comes next.

sections.heading: Advancing how the world understands AI
sections.text: Wharton is the undisputed research powerhouse among business schools. Our 240+ faculty members are studying AI’s impact on everything from monetary policy, to career progression, to medical decision-making—and bringing new insights directly into the classroom. We created the Wharton AI Research Fund to support faculty in further exploring how AI is being applied and its human impact. The AI Education Innovation Fund provides faculty with resources to develop new AI courses, enhance existing curricula, and create innovative learning experiences.

sections.heading: AI in Our Lives: The Behavioral Science of Autonomous Technology
sections.text: Taught by Stefano Puntoni, Sebastian S. Kresge Professor of Marketing and Faculty Co-Director of Wharton Human-AI Research, this class examines the ways AI impacts individuals, organizations, and society, offering students a chance to critically assess both the benefits and risks of this rapidly evolving technology.

items.name: Cait Lamberton
items.title: Professor of Marketing, Vice Dean, Undergraduate Division
items.quote: Our role is to help students develop the discipline to learn first, because AI can be a tempting shortcut, and then move from superficial efficiency toward deeper, creative use.

items.name: Michael Roberts
items.title: Professor of Finance, Vice Dean, MBA Program
items.quote: AI can run the numbers, but it cannot necessarily tell us whether to believe them, what to do with them, or how to live with the consequences. Wharton’s value is teaching how to use knowledge well.

items.name: Kevin Werbach
items.title: Professor of Legal Studies & Business Ethics, Vice Dean, Executive MBA Program
items.quote: [The Executive MBA] program gives [our students] dedicated time—in class, during in-person weekends and through assignments—to wrestle with where AI can automate work and make life easier, and where they should double down on the value they uniquely provide as human beings.

items.name: Nancy Zhang
items.title: Professor of Statistics and Data Science, Vice Dean, Doctoral Programs
items.quote: AI can accelerate discovery, but it cannot replace the rigor of asking the right question, testing assumptions, and making the work transparent. Our job is to prepare scholars to use these tools with curiosity, discipline, and accountability.

sections.heading: Student Experience
sections.text: At Wharton, AI isn’t treated as an elective—it’s viewed as a core business competency and embedded throughout our students’ learning experience. We were the first leading business school to create a dedicated AI MBA major and undergraduate concentration. Our Artificial Intelligence for Business Curriculum explores the technical skills needed to work with and evaluate AI systems, along with the business, economic, legal, ethical, psychological, and societal impacts of AI. Outside the classroom, our AI & Analytics Accelerator pairs students with industry experts to explore real-world business challenges and develop solutions using the latest techniques in machine learning and AI. Students further explore their interests in AI through nearly a dozen AI and Analytics clubs and our annual Wharton Hack-AI-thon.

items.description: Our AI insights extend to professionals around the world through a portfolio of AI and Analytics Programs for Executives. At the other end of the learning spectrum, pre-collegiate students gain exposure to valuable AI skills through the Wharton Global Youth Program.

items.title: AI Infrastructure
items.description: As one of the first business schools to make bold investments in generative AI, we challenged our entire community to think differently about what it means to teach, learn, and live in an AI-enabled world. We are continuously expanding our portfolio of AI tools so that every student, faculty, and staff member can experiment in a safe and secure environment.

items.title: A Global Community of AI Leaders
items.description: Wharton has the largest business school alumni network on the planet. This community of 108,000+ leaders is deeply engaged with our students, sharing their real-world experience and perspectives on how their firms and industries are harnessing AI in real time.

sections.heading: The Power of Penn’s AI Community
sections.text: Wharton’s approach to AI is strengthened by its place within the University of Pennsylvania, where expertise across 12 schools expands what our faculty and learners can explore. Wharton brings the business perspective—connecting advances in AI with the leadership, judgment, and accountability required to put them to work responsibly.
